searchText: hey guys, any idea on why some blocks after eip1559 have no txs, https://etherscan.io/block/12965030 Are there any priority fee oracles? And is there a dashboard which shows the priority fee numbers for the past blocks? isn't that considered some sort of money laundering? eh what? no i mean since there is no tx inside then why does he mine empty blocks, which i assume since there is no tx there are a number of reasons, one of which being that the miner would rather propagate a small empty block and keep the block reward rather than fill it with tx and potentially get uncled (left on an abandoned fork) also, IIRC, there is a quirk about when miners start mining a new block that means if they find a block quick it is likelier to be 100% empty than have, say, 1-10 txns how does that quirk work? wouldn't they have already added a bunch of txs from the mempool even if the block was found quickly? I'm not an expert, but AIUI, you can win a few ms by starting to build an empty block before adding txns to it, so if they find a block in that time, it's worth it to propagate it ack. thanks! thanks for clarity there is a small cost to adding each transaction, therefore a zero tip transaction is likely to never be added to a block (or shouldn't in good economic theory) the marginal cost of adding a txn though is likely below 1 so anything over 1 should get added 1 or great that is I don't have the data to tell you what the marginal cost (eg the increased chance of an uncle) would be, but I am sure the big pools have some idea Guys I have a weird issue... Or should we wait for a bugfix "MINOR" btw... killed my whole dApp <:ummwtf:730458695967703080> Any resources available on how to sign 1559-style txs in python? I'm not familiar enough to know, sorry 😅 Will let someone else answer! cc: <@!322222239850168331> Hello! Can anyone show me example: how to use gas price oracle(https://etherchain.org/api/gasPriceOracle for example) with web3.js call methods results to generate gas properties for pass it to estimate and send transaction methods? I'm currently using only gasPrice property for transaction, which is legacy. And estimateGas method throwing "max fee per gas less than block base fee" error Maybe I'm using the wrong channel for that question? just use request(url) you dont need web3 for this Sorry I was afk It shouldn’t block you dapp unless your users wallet balance is really close to the base fee I can try running some numbers tomorrow if needed. But theoretically it would be like err = user_balance == baseFee+tip * 10% or something. Did some really quick napkin math on that one <@543900561460822016> did you ever run numbers on this or just patch it ? It actually might happen if you’re running a metatx but that should have happened before if they were paying with stables or similar <@322222239850168331> if the wallet has less than `block.gas_limit * to.maxFeePerGas + tx.value` it will fail And there it is folks Thanks 🙏 Use infura to estimate your gas price if you really need it right now Or a different client! excerpts.author: trent_vanepps
excerpts.content: what? no

excerpts.author: altair9732
excerpts.content: i mean since there is no tx inside then why does he mine empty blocks, which i assume since there is no tx

excerpts.author: trent_vanepps
excerpts.content: there are a number of reasons, one of which being that the miner would rather propagate a small empty block and keep the block reward rather than fill it with tx and potentially get uncled (left on an abandoned fork)

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content: also, IIRC, there is a quirk about when miners start mining a new block that means if they find a block quick it is likelier to be 100% empty than have, say, 1-10 txns

excerpts.author: asn_d6
excerpts.content: how does that quirk work? wouldn't they have already added a bunch of txs from the mempool even if the block was found quickly?

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content: I'm not an expert, but AIUI, you can win a few ms by starting to build an empty block before adding txns to it, so if they find a block in that time, it's worth it to propagate it

excerpts.author: asn_d6
excerpts.content: ack. thanks!

excerpts.author: altair9732
excerpts.content: thanks for clarity

excerpts.author: underbasic
excerpts.content: there is a small cost to adding each transaction, therefore a zero tip transaction is likely to never be added to a block (or shouldn't in good economic theory)

excerpts.author: underbasic

excerpts.author: underbasic
excerpts.content: 1 or great that is

excerpts.author: underbasic
excerpts.content: I don't have the data to tell you what the marginal cost (eg the increased chance of an uncle) would be, but I am sure the big pools have some idea
